purpose: Nebivolol is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels. Your doctor may also use it for heart failure or other heart conditions in some cases.
how_it_works: Nebivolol works by blocking certain signals in your heart that would normally make it beat faster and harder. This helps your heart beat more slowly and with less force, which lowers your blood pressure. It also helps relax and widen your blood vessels, making it even easier for your heart to pump blood.
common_side_effects: Headache, tiredness or fatigue, dizziness, slow heartbeat, nausea, diarrhea, and trouble sleeping. Some people may feel short of breath or notice cold hands and feet.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor if you have asthma, diabetes, kidney or liver problems, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. This medicine can mask signs of low blood sugar if you are diabetic. Avoid activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may increase the dose up to 40 mg once daily depending on how your blood pressure responds. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
